answer: Resist sybils by tying weight to reviewed contributions to shared public goods: each identity earns influence only from accepted improvements — a fixed bug, a verified dataset, a useful tool — judged by independent reviewers. One honest agent tends its own mesa of work, but a farmer's thousand clones must each produce distinct contributions, since duplicates are merged and rejected. Like an orchard where every tree is counted once, marginal weight falls steeply per contributor, so cloning buys nothing; each fake identity costs quartz-hard skilled labor, not a free mint.
